stableMappingPatterns.name: Date normalization: unadjustedDate -> adjustableDate.unadjustedDate (YYYY-MM-DD)
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Dates from multiple FpML examples are copied into CDM unadjusted date fields after removing timezone and trimming to date (YYYY-MM-DD).
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM fields expect date-only values; repeated examples show timezone-stripping and formatting applied deterministically.
caveats: Some datetime inputs include timezones and times - transformation removes timezone and time component.
Ensure resulting value is validated as ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

stableMappingPatterns.name: Party reference resolution: swapstream payer/receiver href -> interestratepayout.payerreceiver.payer|receiver
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Party hrefs are consistently resolved into CDM payer/receiver role entries. Multiple examples show this resolution and that the order/assignment may be inverted relative to the raw href order.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: FpML uses href references to identify payer/receiver; CDM represents explicit payer/receiver role objects, so hrefs are mapped to those objects. Repeated examples indicate a consistent mapping rule was applied (with inversion in some outputs).
caveats: Several outputs show the payer/receiver assignment reversed versus the original hrefs - treat inversion as active behavior to investigate rather than an isolated error.
Mapping should preserve party identity (externalKey/partyId) even when role assignment appears inverted.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Trade identifier copy: tradeHeader.tradeId -> assignedIdentifier.identifier.value
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: FpML tradeId values are repeatedly copied into CDM assignedIdentifier/identifier.value fields.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Trade identifiers are preserved to maintain traceability; examples show direct copying of FpML tradeId into CDM identifier structures.
caveats: CDM may include additional identifier metadata (scheme) not present in the FpML field - mapping preserves core id value but external scheme population may vary.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Payer/receiver role inversion
variantsAndExceptions.description: Although party hrefs are resolved into CDM payer/receiver roles consistently, multiple examples show the CDM payer/receiver assignment is reversed relative to the FpML href ordering.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Mapping logic should account for possible systematic inversion; do not assume first href -> payer without verifying role semantics. Treat inversion as an important exception to validate.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Unmapped bondReference
variantsAndExceptions.description: Some FpML fields such as bondReference appear in inputs but do not have an obvious CDM target in the provided examples.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Fields without repeated mapping evidence should be treated as exceptions; avoid inventing CDM targets without additional mappings or stakeholder guidance.
